'" "And Hashem appeared to him" (Genesis 18:1).
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מח, א): דָּבָר אַחֵר: "אִם אֶמְאַס מִשְׁפַּט עַבְדִּי וַאֲמָתִי" (אִיּוֹב לא, יג) – זֶה אַבְרָהָם
, In Midrash Rabbah (Parashah 48:1): Another interpretation: "'If I despised the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant' (Job 31:13) – this refers to Abraham,
דִּכְתִיב: "וַיִּקַּח אַבְרָהָם אֶת יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יז, כג
), as it is written: 'And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house... and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin' (Genesis 17:23),
אִלּוּלֵי שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי כֵּן מֵהֵיכָן הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִגְלֶה עָלַי? וְכוּלֵי
. saying: 'Had I not done so, from where would the Holy One, blessed be He, have been revealed to me?' etc."
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה שַּׁיָּיכוּת מִילַת יִשְׁמָעֵאל, שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁאִלּוּלֵי שֶׁמָּל אֶת יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לְהִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה
? We must understand what connection the circumcision of Ishmael has to this, such that Abraham declared that had he not circumcised Ishmael, he would not have been worthy of this divine revelation.
וּלְמַעְלָה אָמַר: "'וּמִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ' – אִלּוּלֵי שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי כֵּן מֵהֵיכָן הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִגְלֶה עָלַי

", Earlier in the Midrash it stated: "'And from my flesh I shall behold God' (Job 19:26) – had I not done so (circumcised myself), from where would the Holy One, blessed be He, have been revealed to me?"—
יִתָּכֵן שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַמִּילָה זָכָה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה
'", and it is reasonable that through his own circumcision he merited the revelation of "And Hashem appeared to him";
אֲבָל מִילַת יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁיִּגְרוֹם זֶה אֵינוֹ מוּבָן
. however, that the circumcision of Ishmael should bring this about is incomprehensible.
גַּם לְבַד זֶה, כְּבָר הִקְשׁוּ גַּם לְמַעְלָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם קוֹדֶם הַמִּילָה כְּתִיב שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים "וַיֵּרָא ה' אֶל אַבְרָם
". Furthermore, aside from this, we already raised the difficulty above (in Discourse 1) that even prior to the circumcision it is written twice, "And Hashem appeared to Abram."

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayera 1:10-13: “Rather, it is a concealed mystery: “Hashem appeared to him”—to that level which spoke with him, something that had not occurred previously, before he was circumcised. Now voice was revealed and joined with speech when He spoke with him. “And he was sitting at the entrance of the tent”: “he,” without revealing who. Here wisdom is revealed: all the levels rested upon this lower level after Avraham was circumcised. Come and see: “Hashem appeared to him”—this is the mystery of the audible voice joining with speech and being revealed in it. “And he was sitting at the entrance of the tent”: this is the upper world, standing to illuminate him. “In the heat of the day”: the right side shone forth, the level of Avraham, to which he cleaved. Another interpretation: “in the heat of the day”—when one level drew near another, in their longing for one another. “He appeared to him.” Rabbi Abba said: Before Avraham was circumcised he was sealed. Once he was circumcised, everything was revealed, and the Shechinah rested upon him completely, as is fitting. Come and see: “And he was sitting at the entrance of the tent.” “He”: this is the upper world resting upon this lower world. When? “In the heat of the day”—when the desire of one righteous one is to dwell in it.”

p: אֲבָל כְּבָר עָמַד עַל זֶה בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (וַיֵּרָא צח עַמּוּד א
): However, the holy Zohar (Vayera 98a) has already addressed this question: "
דְּאִי לְאַבְרָהָם, מַאי שְׁבָחָא הָא יַתִּיר מִבְּקַדְמֵיתָא עַד דְּלָא אִתְגְּזַר וְכוּלֵי
? "For if 'to him' (elav) merely means to Abraham, what greater praise is this than beforehand when he was not yet circumcised, etc.?
אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי דְּהַשְׁתָּא אִתְגְּלֵי קוֹל וְאִתְחַבַּר בְּדִבּוּר כַּד מַלִּיל עִמֵּיהּ", עַיֵּין שָׁם
. Rather, etc., now the supernal Voice (Kol) was revealed and united with Speech (Dibbur) when He spoke with him," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשָׁם כְּתִיב "וַיֵּרָא ה' אֶל אַבְרָם", וְהַיְינוּ לְנֶפֶשׁ אַבְרָם
, The explanation is that prior to circumcision it is written, "And Hashem appeared to Abram," referring strictly to the Nefesh (vital soul) of Abram—
שֶׁחַיּוּת הָאָדָם הוּא שְׁמוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּסְּפָרִים הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁהָאָב מְכַוֵּין בִּקְרִיאַת שֵׁם בְּנוֹ לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּת שֶׁל הַבֵּן
, for a person's vital life-force (Nefesh) is invested in his name, as is written in the holy books that when a father names his son, he unconsciously aligns with the root of the son's vitality,
וְכֵן רוֹאִים שֶׁבִּקְרִיאַת שֵׁם הָאָדָם נֵיעוֹר מִשְּׁנָתוֹ
. and we likewise observe empirically that calling a person's name awakens him from sleep.
וְכָאן כְּתִיב "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה'" – אֶל י' ו
', Whereas here (after circumcision) it is written, "And Hashem appeared to him (
אֵלָיו
)" – which spells
אֶל י' ו
' (unto the Yud and the Vav);
דְּמַדְרֵגוֹת נֶפֶשׁ רוּחַ נְשָׁמָה חַיָּה יְחִידָה הֵם נֶגֶד ד' אוֹתִיּוֹת הֲוָיָ"ה וְקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּכָל מָקוֹם
; for the five soul-levels of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah correspond to the four letters of the Tetragrammaton (
ה-ו-ה-י
from below to above) and the upper thorn of the Yud, as is written everywhere;
וְכָאן זָכָה שֶׁהַהִתְגַּלּוּת הָיָה לְהָרוּחַ שֶׁהוּא מֵאוֹת וָ"ו שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם, שֶׁהוּא "הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן וְגוֹמֵר
", and here he merited that the divine revelation reached the level of Ruach, which stems from the letter Vav of the Divine Name (Tiferet), "the middle bar that passes through from end to end,"
וְיוּ"ד – חָכְמָה, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם נִשְׁמְתָא לְנִשְׁמְתָא (חַיָּה) שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ לְהֵ"א עִלָּאָה (בִּינָה
), and the letter Yud – Chokhmah (Wisdom), whence stems the soul of the soul (Chayah) which illuminates the upper Hei (Binah, the root of Neshamah and the heart),
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי תָבוֹא חָכְמָה בְלִבֶּךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי ב, י
), in accordance with what is stated: "For wisdom (Chokhmah / Yud) shall enter into your heart (Binah / upper Hei), etc." (Proverbs 2:10),
וּמוֹפִיעַ לְהֵ"א תַּתָּאָה (מַלְכוּת) שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הַנֶּפֶשׁ
. and through the Vav it illuminates down to the lower Hei (Malchut), whence stems the Nefesh.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר: "דְּהַשְׁתָּא אִתְגְּלֵי קוֹל וְאִתְחַבַּר לְדִבּוּר
", And this is what the Zohar meant: "that now the supernal Voice (Kol / Vav) was revealed and united with Speech (Dibbur / lower Hei),"
וְהוּא שֶׁהַקּוֹל חַיּוּת הַדִּבּוּר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ג עַמּוּד א): "קוֹל אָתֵי לְדִבּוּר וְכוּלֵי
"; because the Voice is the inner vitality of Speech, as is written (Zohar Part II, 3a): "Voice comes to animate Speech, etc.";
וּמִקּוֹדֶם זָכָה רַק לְדִבּוּר שֶׁהוּא מִמִּדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א לב עַמּוּד א): "שַׁבָּת דִּבּוּר אִקְרֵי
", for prior to circumcision he merited only the level of Speech (Dibbur), which emanates from the final attribute (Malchut), as is written (Zohar Part I, 32a): "Shabbat (Malchut) is called Dibbur,"
וְכָאן זָכָה לְקוֹל – חַיּוּת שֶׁל הַדִּבּוּר
; whereas here he merited the supernal Voice—the inner life-force of Speech;
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֵלָיו" – אֶל י' ו', תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, ו' תִּפְאֶרֶת י' חָכְמָה
. and this is alluded to in the word
אֵלָיו
(to him) –
אֶל י' ו
' (unto Yud and Vav), representing the Written Torah (Vav / Tiferet) illuminated by Chokhmah (Yud).

p: וְהִנֵּה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ הַפְּסוֹלֶת
– Now, so long as unrectified dross (pesolet) remained attached to Abraham—
שֶׁאַף שֶׁיִּצְחָק לֹא נוֹלַד עֲדַיִן וְלֹא הָיָה פְּסוֹלֶת שֶׁל עֵשָׂו
, for even though Isaac had not yet been born and thus the dross of Esau had not yet been separated out,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם פְּסוֹלֶת שֶׁל יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא יָצָא עֲדַיִן, שֶׁעֲדַיִן נֶחְשָׁב לְזַרְעוֹ
, nevertheless, the dross of Ishmael had already emerged from him and was still reckoned as his seed,
וְרַק אַחַר כָּךְ נִתְבָּרֵר "כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כא, יב), וְ"לֹא כָּל יִצְחָק" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (נְדָרִים לא.) שֶׁיִּשְׁמָעֵאל וְעֵשָׂו אֵינָם נֶחְשָׁבִים זַרְעוֹ

; and only later was it clarified, "for in Isaac shall seed be called to you" (Genesis 21:12)—expounded (Nedarim 31a) as "in Isaac, and not all of Isaac," teaching that Ishmael and Esau are ultimately excluded from being reckoned as his seed;
אֲבָל כָּאן כְּתִיב: "לוּ יִשְׁמָעֵאל יִחְיֶה לְפָנֶיךָ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יז, יח), וְאַף דִּכְתִיב: "וְאֶת בְּרִיתִי אָקִים אֶת יִצְחָק", מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל נֶחְשָׁב עוֹד בִּכְלַל זַרְעוֹ

– yet at this point, when Abraham prayed "O that Ishmael might live before You!" (Genesis 17:18), even though God replied "My covenant I will establish with Isaac," Ishmael was nonetheless still included within his seed—
וְלֹא הָיָה זוֹכֶה עֲדַיִן לְמַעֲלָה זוֹ (אִם הָיָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל נִשְׁאָר בְּעָרְלָתוֹ
). therefore, Abraham could not have merited this supernal revelation of
אֵלָיו
had Ishmael remained uncircumcised.
אַךְ כְּתִיב: "וּלְיִשְׁמָעֵאל שְׁמַעְתִּיךָ הִנֵּה בֵּרַכְתִּי אֹתוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם יז, כ), וּבְרָכָה שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִיא בְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
, However, it is written: "And as for Ishmael, I have heard you; behold, I have blessed him, etc." (Genesis 17:20), and a blessing from Hashem, blessed be He, pertains to eternal spiritual life,
וּבֶאֱמֶת לֹא הָיָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל עֲדַיִן מְקוּלְקָל אָז
. and in truth Ishmael had not yet corrupted his ways at that time.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּקַּח אַבְרָהָם אֶת יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ... בְּעֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" (שָׁם יז, כג
), And this is the meaning of what is stated: "And Abraham took Ishmael his son... in the selfsame day (be'etzem ha-yom ha-zeh)" (Genesis 17:23),
וּכְתִיב: "בְּעֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה נִמּוֹל אַבְרָהָם וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ" (שָׁם יז, כו
). and it is repeated: "In the selfsame day (be'etzem ha-yom ha-zeh) was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his son" (Genesis 17:26). "
הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" מוֹרֶה עַל אוֹר, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם" (שָׁם א, ה
); The phrase "this day" (ha-yom ha-zeh) signifies spiritual light, in accordance with what is stated: "And God called the light Day" (Genesis 1:5);
וְ"הַזֶּה" מוֹרֶה שֶׁהָאוֹר מְפוֹרָשׁ עַד שֶׁיּוּכַל לִהְיוֹת מַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד ("הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ זֶה

"), and the demonstrative word "this" (ha-zeh) indicates that the illumination is so explicit and tangible that one can point to it with his finger, as in the future redemption ("Behold, this zeh is our God"),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָאוֹר נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב, שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה לְשׁוֹן "זֶה
". meaning that the divine light becomes firmly fixed within the heart, which is what the word "zeh" denotes.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה וְאוֹר בְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל עַל יְדֵי הַמִּילָה
. Thus, Abraham our father, peace be upon him, infused sanctity and divine light into Ishmael through the act of circumcision.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ: "'אִם אֶמְאַס מִשְׁפַּט עַבְדִּי' – וַיִּקַּח אַבְרָהָם אֶת יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ וְגוֹמֵר", וְסָמִיךְ עַל סוֹף הַכָּתוּב: "בְּעֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה

"; And this is what the Midrash meant in citing: "'If I despised the cause of my manservant' – 'And Abraham took Ishmael his son, etc.,'" relying upon the conclusion of the verse: "in the selfsame day (be'etzem ha-yom ha-zeh)";
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "אִלּוּלֵי שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי כֵּן" – שֶׁהָיָה מַכְנִיס אוֹר בְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל – "מֵהֵיכָן הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִגְלֶה עָלַי
?" and thus Abraham declared: "Had I not done so"—infusing this light of circumcision into Ishmael—"from where would the Holy One, blessed be He, have been revealed to me?"
כֵּיוָן שֶׁנֶּחְשַׁב אָז מִזַּרְעוֹ, הָיָה מְנִיעָה מִצַּד יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יָכוֹל לִזְכּוֹת לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ דְּ"וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו" שֶׁמּוֹרֶה אֶל י' ו' כָּאָמוּר

. For since Ishmael was then still reckoned as part of his seed, had Ishmael remained uncircumcised there would have been an impediment on Ishmael's account preventing Abraham from attaining this lofty level of "And He appeared to him (
אֵלָיו
)"—signifying
אֶל י' ו
' as explained above.

p: וּמִקּוֹדֶם אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (שָׁם): "'וַתִּתֶּן לִי מָגֵן יִשְׁעֶךָ' (תְּהִלִּים יח, לו) – זֶה אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵי, 'וְעַנְוַתְךָ תַּרְבֵּנִי

' – Earlier in that same passage in Midrash Rabbah (48:1) it states: "'And You have given me the shield of Your salvation' (Psalms 18:36) – this refers to Abraham, etc.; 'and Your humility has made me great' –
מָה עֲנָוָה הִרְבָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם? שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב וְהַשְּׁכִינָה עוֹמֶדֶת, הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה' וְהוּא יֹשֵׁב
". what humility did the Holy One, blessed be He, lavish upon Abraham? That he was sitting while the Shechinah was standing, as it is written: 'And Hashem appeared to him... and he was sitting.'"
וְלִכְאוֹרָה לֹא נִרְמַז כָּאן שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה עוֹמֶדֶת
? Seemingly, where is there any hint in the verse that the Shechinah was standing?
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן דִּכְתִיב: "עַד דִּי כָרְסָוָן רְמִיו וְעַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב" (דָּנִיֵּאל ז, ט
), However, the explanation is based on what is written: "Until thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days (Atik Yomin) did sit" (Daniel 7:9),
וּכְשֶׁיֵּשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא – יוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא
– teaching that when there is a manifestation of Atika (the aspect of Keter), He is depicted as "sitting upon the Throne";
אָז "אֵין יְשִׁיבָה בָּעֲזָרָה אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד בִּלְבַד", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא כה
.). and in the presence of that revelation, human sitting is impossible, as they taught (Yoma 25a): "Sitting in the Temple Courtyard is permitted only to the kings of the House of David alone."

וְהוּא דְּבַגְּמָרָא (חֲגִיגָה יד.) עַל "כָרְסָוָן רְמִיו": "אֶחָד לוֹ וְאֶחָד לְדָוִד וְכוּלֵי", וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא: "אֶחָד לְכִסֵּא וְאֶחָד לְשַׁרְפְּרַף וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: הַשָּׁמַיִם כִּסְאִי וְהָאָרֶץ הֲדֹם רַגְלָי" (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, א

). And this connects to what is taught in the Gemara (Chagigah 14a) on the plural "thrones were placed": Rabbi Akiva initially said "one for Him and one for David," and subsequently accepted the explanation "one for a throne and one for a footstool, as it is stated: 'The heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool'" (Isaiah 66:1).
וְאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהַכֹּל אֶחָד, שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת
, And we have explained elsewhere that both statements mean the exact same thing: for King David, peace be upon him, was the chariot for the attribute of Malchut,
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָאָרֶץ הֲדֹם רַגְלָי" – אֶרֶץ דְּאִיקְרֵי כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל (מַלְכוּת), כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א לא רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב
). and this is the meaning of "and the earth is My footstool"—for "earth" is a title of Knesset Yisrael (Malchut), as is written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 31b top).
וּבְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה, נִקְרָא "בֵּית הֲדֹם רַגְלֵי אֱלֹהֵינוּ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַכּוֹת כד סוֹף עַמּוּד א

); Thus the Holy Temple (specifically the Courtyard), where there is the revelation of the Shechinah (Malchut, the footstool), is called "the house of the footstool of our God" (I Chronicles 28:2), as cited in Makkot (24a end)—and there the kings of the House of David, who embody Malchut, may sit;
וּבְבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁיֵּשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא – "עַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב", יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא
, whereas within the Holy of Holies, where there is the revelation of Atika—"the Ancient of Days did sit," sitting upon the supernal Throne,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת ז.) "וָאֶרְאֶה אֶת ה' יֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רָם וְנִשָּׂא" וְנִזְכָּר שָׁם שֵׁם שֶׁל כֶּתֶר, עַיֵּין שָׁם – וְשָׁם אֵין יְשִׁיבָה כְּלָל

. as referenced in the Gemara (Berakhot 7a) when the High Priest entered the Holy of Holies and beheld Akhtariel Yah (the Name corresponding to Keter, see there) sitting upon a high and exalted throne—there no human sitting is possible at all.

וְאִם הָיָה זוֹכֶה אָז בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת "עַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב" – יוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא – לֹא הָיָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יוֹשֵׁב

. so if in this revelation he had already merited the manifestation of "the Ancient of Days did sit" (Atika sitting upon the Throne), Abraham our father, peace be upon him, could not have been sitting.
אַךְ לֹא זָכָה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא עַד אַחַר נִסְיוֹן הָעֲקֵידָה, דִּכְתִיב: "וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים וַה' בֵּרַךְ אֶת אַבְרָהָם בַּכֹּל" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כד, א

); However, he did not merit the revelation of Atika (Keter) until after the trial of the Akeidah, when it is written: "And Abraham was old (zaken, corresponding to Atik Yomin), well-advanced in days" (Genesis 24:1);
וְכָאן אַחַר הַמִּילָה זָכָה רַק לְ"וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו", שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ מֵאוֹת י' ו' לְמִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה – "וְהָאָרֶץ הֲדֹם רַגְלָי
", whereas here, immediately after the circumcision, he merited only "And He appeared to him (
אֵלָיו

)," which alludes to the illumination shining from the letters Yud and Vav down to the final attribute (Malchut)—"and the earth is My footstool" (where the Shechinah is depicted as standing, extending His feet to the footstool)—
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי הָיָה הוּא "יוֹשֵׁב פֶּתַח הָאֹהֶל", שֶׁהוּא הַפֶּתַח לִזְכּוֹת לְאוֹר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא הָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁזָּכוּ אָז לְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא

. and for this reason Abraham was able to be "sitting at the entrance of the tent," which represents the gateway (Malchut) toward eventually meriting the light of the Giving of the Torah—the "great substance" wherein Israel merited the revelation of Atika.

. The Midrash continues: "'And Your right hand has sustained me' – in the fiery furnace, in the famine, and against the four kings," see there.

: This is understood based on what they stated (Berakhot 6a): "'By His right hand' – this refers to the Torah (as in 'From His right hand went a fiery law for them')," for these three miraculous deliverances signify the three dimensions of Torah:
כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ דְּאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים – שָׁם הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁבְּבָבֶל עִיקַּר יְסוֹדָהּ (כְּשֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים

); 1) The fiery furnace of Ur Kasdim (in Babylonia) – there lay the root of the Oral Torah (the Babylonian Talmud), whose primary foundation was established in Babylonia (as we have explained several times);
בָּרְעָבוֹן יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם – וְשָׁם הָיָה בְּגָלוּת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם זָכוּ לְהָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוּא מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וְהָיָה בְּמִצְרַיִם בְּגָלוּת בְּחָכְמַת מִצְרַיִם

; 2) In the famine he descended to Egypt – where the sparks of the Written Torah were held in exile amidst the wisdom of Egypt, and from which Israel emerged with "great substance" to receive the Torah at Sinai;
וּבַמְּלָכִים – שָׁם הִצִּיל אֶת לוֹט שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל בּוֹ נֶפֶשׁ דָּוִד שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ, וְזֶה מוֹרֶה עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁעָתִיד לְגַלּוֹת

, 3) And in the war of the kings – there he rescued Lot, within whom was contained the soul of King David who descended from him, signifying the Torah of the Messiah which he is destined to reveal in the future,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה יא, ח): "כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁאַתָּה לָמֵד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֶבֶל הוּא לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא", וְהַיְינוּ לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ

. concerning which they stated in the Midrash (Kohelet Rabbah 11:8): "All the Torah that you learn in this world is vanity compared to the Torah of the World to Come," referring to the days of the Messiah.

וְכֵן נִזְכְּרוּ אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים יַחַד בַּעֲצַת מַמְרֵא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (תּוֹסֶפְתָּא צח עַמּוּד ב): "אָמַר לֵיהּ מַמְרֵא: דְּכַרְתְּ וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם שֶׁזָּכַר כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ וּמִצְרַיִם וּמְלָכִים

, Indeed, these very three events are mentioned together in the counsel of Mamre to Abraham in the holy Zohar (Tosefta, Vayera 98b): "Mamre said to him: Do you remember when you were saved from the fiery furnace, from Egypt, and from the kings? etc.," see there,
וְהַיְינוּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמּוֹרִים עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה חֶלְקֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה: תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְתוֹרָה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
. precisely because they correspond to the three divisions of Torah: the Written Torah, the Oral Torah, and the Torah of the Messiah.

p: וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וִימִינְךָ תִּסְעָדֵנִי" – "בִּימִינוֹ" זוֹ תּוֹרָה, וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם חֶסֶד דְּרוֹעָא יְמִינָא, וּמִמֶּנּוּ הִתְחִיל הַשְּׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה

, And this is the meaning of "And Your right hand has sustained me"—for "His right hand" is the Torah, and Abraham our father, peace be upon him, embodies Chesed, the right arm, and with him began the middle two-thousand-year era of Torah (Avodah Zarah 9a),
וְזָכָה לְכָל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרִים שְׁלֹשָׁה נִסִּים אֵלּוּ
, and he merited all three dimensions of Torah signified by these three miracles,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לִהְיוֹת הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה – "וְהָאָרֶץ הֲדֹם רַגְלָי", וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "וְהַשְּׁכִינָה עוֹמֶדֶת
". and through this he merited the revelation of the Shechinah in the aspect of "and the earth is My footstool," which is what the Midrash calls "and the Shechinah was standing."
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ: "'וְעַנְוַתְךָ תַּרְבֵּנִי' וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁלִּזְכּוֹת לְכָל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה זוֹכִין רַק עַל יְדֵי עֲנָוָה
, And this is why the Midrash connects this to the phrase "'and Your humility has made me great,' etc.," because to merit all the words of Torah is possible solely through humility,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת הַתּוֹרָה עַל שְׁמוֹ, וּכְתִיב: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו מְאֹד" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יב, ג
). just as we find regarding Moses our teacher, after whom the Torah is named, of whom it is written: "And the man Moses was exceedingly humble" (Numbers 12:3).
וּמַסִּיק: "מָה עֲנָוָה הִרְבָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁזָּכָה לְמִדַּת עֲנָוָה
, And the Midrash concludes: "What humility did the Holy One, blessed be He, lavish upon Abraham, etc.," meaning that because Abraham attained the attribute of humility ("I am but dust and ashes"),
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ מִי' חָכְמָה ו' קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְמִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה
, through this he merited the revelation of the Shechinah shining from Yud (Chokhmah) and Vav (the Holy One, blessed be He) down to the final attribute (Malchut),
וְזָכָה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה עוֹמֶדֶת, וְעַל כֵּן "וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב
". meriting the manifestation of the Shechinah "standing" ("My footstool"), and therefore "he was sitting."

אֲבָל אִם הָיָה זוֹכֶה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת "וְעַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב" כְּמוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה אַחַר נִסְיוֹן הָעֲקֵידָה דִּכְתִיב "וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן", אָז לֹא הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב, שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ הָיָה "אַתָּה כֹהֵן וְגוֹמֵר

". Whereas had he then merited the higher revelation of "and the Ancient of Days did sit" (Atika), as he merited after the trial of the Akeidah where it is written "And Abraham was old," he could not have been sitting, since his personal station was "You are a priest forever" (and in that realm only the Davidic king sits).
וְזֶה דְּמַסִּיק: "הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: וַיֵּרָא אֵלָי"ו" דַּיְיקָא, וּמַה שֶּׁזָּכָה לָזֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת עֲנָוָה
. And this is why the Midrash concludes carefully: "Thus it is written: 'And He appeared
אֵלָיו
(to him)'" specifically (denoting
אֶל י' ו
' illuminating Malchut), and his meriting this was likewise through the attribute of humility.
